title: Generating a receipt spend snapshot image
scenario: A personal budgeting app lets a user upload two receipt photos (groceries and a utility bill) and generates a single infographic-style summary image via Gemini's image model through the Vercel AI SDK, for the user to paste into a paper budgeting notebook.

content.text:
I'm attaching two photos: my grocery receipt from this weekend and my
electricity bill for the month. I want you to generate a single square
graphic I can drop into my budget notebook that visually summarizes both,
instead of me typing the numbers into a spreadsheet by hand again.

Please make it look like a clean infographic card, not a photo collage:
- A header that says "Monthly Spend Snapshot"
- A small subheader underneath with just the month and year, nothing
  else identifying, so I can reuse the same layout every month
- Two stacked bars or blocks, one for "Groceries" and one for "Utilities",
  sized roughly proportional to what's on each receipt (groceries is the
  bigger one this month, utilities is smaller but still significant
  compared to last month's bill, which was noticeably lower)
- Small icons next to each category (a shopping basket for groceries, a
  lightning bolt for utilities) instead of showing the actual receipt text
  or any line items from either photo
- A muted, paper-like background so it doesn't look like a screenshot
  pasted onto a page, more like something hand-drawn for a notebook
- Keep all dollar figures approximate and rounded to the nearest ten, I
  don't need exact cents reproduced anywhere on the image, this is just
  for a quick visual reference, not for filing anything official
- No logos, store names, addresses, card numbers, or barcodes from either
  receipt should appear anywhere in the final graphic, just the category
  totals and the two icons I described above
- Use a calm color palette (soft greens and blues) so it matches the rest
  of my budgeting notebook pages, which all use that same palette
- If there's room, add a tiny footer line noting this was generated from
  a photo and might be slightly off

If the electricity bill photo is too blurry to read the total reliably,
just estimate based on what's legible and note that it's approximate in
a small caption at the bottom of the card instead of guessing silently
and presenting it as exact. Same goes for the grocery total if any part
of the receipt is cut off in the photo I sent.
